 View Comments TreVeyon Henderson says he had an "unusual sudden emergency" with "unexplained neurological symptoms." John Tlumacki/Globe Staff FOXBOROUGH — TreVeyon Henderson said Friday he recently underwent an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency,” and as a result, was diagnosed with “unexplainable neurological symptoms.” 
 In a statement posted to Instagram, the Patriots’ running back explained his medical issues, which have impacted his motor skills. A source close to Henderson said he did not suffer a stroke. 
 “I would like to provide an official statement regarding the medical condition I’ve been experiencing,” he wrote. 
 “Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days. During that time I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable. 
 “I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities.

 “I want to thank my wife for being by my side throughout all of this, and most importantly, I want to thank Jesus for giving me a peace that surpasses all understanding. Despite all of this, my heart rejoices in [the] Lord and my heart is at peace knowing that He is always faithful and His promise of Romans 8:28 always remain true. 
 “My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement, and support. We respectfully ask for continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery.” 
 Henderson does have some history with head trauma. As a collegian, he acknowledged he suffered a concussion late in the 2021 season , and had to deal with the side effects for an extended stretch. 
 “I had a concussion,” Henderson said the following year. “I played through that. During the game, I still had the side effects of it. I don’t think I want to talk about what I was going through. But yeah, I played through a concussion. I didn’t really know at first, but I knew. As long as I can run I’ll play through whatever, but I’m going to keep myself safe at the same time.” 
 The 24-year-old Henderson did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday of this week; he was listed on the injury report with an illness. He was first listed on the practice report with an illness on Oct. 29 and missed last Sunday’s game in Miami. 
 Currently in his second season with the Patriots, the former second-round pick out of Ohio State has had a diminished role, with 203 yards on 52 carries and one rushing touchdown, as well as five catches for 45 yards. His last game came against the Bears on Oct. 22, when he had three carries for 9 yards.
